previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for ileal conduit urinary diversion due to severe urinary incontinence causing recurrent skin breakdown and stage IV pressure ulcers. The surgery was performed successfully, and he recovered without intraoperative complications. Post-operatively, he developed a fever on POD4, prompting a CT scan that showed nonspecific post-surgical changes without abscess or pneumonia. Urine culture grew E. coli, leading to a seven-day course of meropenem. His white count improved, and he transitioned from IV to oral pain medication. The NG tube was removed on POD2, diet advanced, and ostomy care was taught. On POD11, ureteral stents and the PICC line were removed, staples were replaced with Steri-Strips, and he was discharged home with visiting nurse services. He refused Bactrim initiation in the hospital but agreed to take it at home. Follow-up was arranged with urology, plastics, and primary care.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with abdominal pain status post loop ileostomy,
recent removal of ureteral stents.  

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from ___.  

TECHNIQUE:  Multi detector CT through the abdomen pelvis performed without IV
or oral contrast with multiplanar reformations provided.  Please note
evaluation is limited due to beam hardening artifact through the upper and mid
abdomen secondary to fusion hardware in the lumbar spine.  

FINDINGS: The imaged lung bases are notable for emphysema without worrisome
nodule, mass, or consolidation.  The imaged portion of the heart is
unremarkable.  There is a small hiatal hernia. 

Abdomen:  Since the prior exam, the bilateral ureteral stents have been
removed and there is severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis.  No stone is seen
along the course of either ureter.  Given the interval removal of the ureteral
stents, please correlate clinically for the possibility of ureteral stricture.


The unenhanced appearance of the liver, spleen, gallbladder, adrenal glands
and pancreas is unremarkable.  The stomach and duodenum appear normal.  The
abdominal aorta is normal in caliber.  No retroperitoneal hematoma or
lymphadenopathy is seen. 

Pelvis: loops of small bowel show no signs of ileus or obstruction.  Suture
along the small bowel in the right lower quadrant appears uncomplicated. 
There are several clips in the lower abdomen and pelvis which relate to prior
ileal conduit surgery.  The colon contains a large fecal load as seen on prior
without evidence of obstruction or thickening.  There is no free pelvic fluid
seen.  The native urinary bladder is decompressed. 

Bones:  Stable appearance of the bones with fusion hardware in the
thoracolumbar junction stabilizing.  An old fracture of T12.  No signs of
hardware failure.  There is chronic dislocation of the left hip and soft
tissue thickening along the right lateral hip which is unchanged from the
prior exam likely postoperative.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Interval removal of bilateral ureteral stents with development of
bilateral hydroureteronephrosis.  Cause of obstruction is not clear as no
definite stone is identified.  Please correlate clinically for underlying
stricture as well as possible infection. 

2.  Postsurgical changes related to ileal conduit urinary diversion.  

3.  Large colonic fecal loading.  

4.  Additional abnormalities, unchanged from prior CT detailed above,
including chronic dislocation of the left hip and chronic fracture deformity
of T12 status post spinal fusion.
